pattern:
This chunk has 13 runs marked wrong, and only 2 are real model misrankings. Both are OWN ownership-displacement variants with the gold at rank 2. In each, the agent displayed the gold, and its own evidence chain states the exact faulty mechanism. It still ranked a co-owner first: the caller that holds the visibly odd null encoding (computeMayUse, Closure-12) or the shared-state reader / decision site (isSimpleNameChars, Closure-131). So the misses are attribution between a writer and its partner on the same causal path, not search failures. In Closure-131 the agent even integrated the cross-file convention (TokenStream.isJSIdentifier) and still preferred the reader.

The other 11 records are not model errors. Ten are provider-stall timeouts (CLOSURE-23-MPO x4, LANG-1-MPO x3, LANG-34-MPO x2, GSON-1-DISC-002 x1). Tool timestamps show normal 4-12 s steps, then silence until the 300 s limit, with the trajectory ending on a tool output and 1-7 API calls made. In 6 of the 10 the gold body was already on screen (all LANG-1, LANG-34 and GSON runs). The four CLOSURE-23 runs never reached Node.getChildAtPosition, although run-019 saw its call site. The last one, Chart-1 run-003, is a harness defect: a corrupt method catalog made the agent rename its correct rank-1 gold answer into catalog garbage class names, and post-hoc validation then rejected those names. These 11 should be excluded or reclassified rather than counted as misses.
